slides.say: Points A, B, C and D lie on a line in this order, as shown in the accompanying figure. Given: A C is eleven, B D is fourteen, and A D is twenty. What is the length of B C?
at: Points A, B, C and D

slides.say: B C is the short piece in the middle, between B and C. [short pause] We'll solve it two ways, finding the pieces one by one, and then with the overlap rule.
at: the short piece in the middle

slides.say: [short pause] The math way first. Let's draw the line again, bigger, and put each length on it. A D is twenty, the whole line from A to D.
at: the whole line from A to D

slides.say: B D is fourteen, the part from B to the end. So what's left at the start, A B, is twenty minus fourteen, which is six.
at: the part from B to the end

slides.say: Now A C is eleven, and A C is made of A B and B C. A B is six, so B C is eleven minus six, which is five. Choice number three is our answer.
at: so B C is eleven minus six
Choice number three is our answer

slides.say: [pause] Now by understanding, with the overlap rule, in one line. Let's draw A C above the line and B D below it.
Together, A C and B D cover the whole line from A to D, and the middle piece, B C, is covered twice. So A C plus B D is the whole line, A D, plus B C one more time.
at: So A C plus B D

slides.say: Eleven plus fourteen is twenty-five, and the whole line is twenty. So twenty-five is twenty plus B C, and B C is five. Choice number three again.

Careful with the other choices. Six, choice number two, is A B, the wrong piece. And twenty-five, choice number four, is A C plus B D, with B C counted twice. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
